lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Scientists just counted wildlife for sale. The number doubled.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At least one hundred seven thousand, three hundred fifty-six species.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That is from a study in the journal Science Advances, reported since late October.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Here is what was counted, what was not, and what nobody knows yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Until now, the number people used was about fifty thousand species.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It came from a twenty twenty-two assessment by an intergovernmental biodiversity panel called IPBES.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The new study puts the count at more than double that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Animals: forty-seven thousand, six hundred eighty-five species.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Plants: at least forty-nine thousand, seven hundred twenty-three, according to the Down To Earth report.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Fungi are counted too. The researchers call it the first global look at how trade in all three is monitored.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Notice the wording. Used or traded.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A broader count of about sixty thousand plant and fungus species includes uses that are not trade at all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So that figure is kept apart from the headline number.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Did trade itself double? The reports do not say that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This is a new count, put together from many databases. A better count, not a report of more trade.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Each database catches a different slice of the species.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now the gap. Few programmes record trade outside the main treaty list, called CITES, and a few sectors such as fisheries.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Even fewer record whether animals were taken from the wild or bred in captivity.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Or whether the use is sustainable.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Only one country, the United States, systematically records and shares trade data across a wide range of species, the university says.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Global biodiversity targets use an indicator to track traded species.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The study estimates that indicator covers about two to three percent of them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The authors warn that more than ninety-eight percent may fall outside some form of international monitoring.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: These are estimates. The team says the real number could be higher, because the data are patchy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Different outlets round the totals a little differently, so the sources are listed below.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The researchers propose standard ways to record trade, electronic permits instead of paper, and automatic checks of shipping documents.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Those are their recommendations. Nothing here has been decided.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Still unknown: how much of this trade is sustainable. The study counts species. It does not say which are in trouble.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: If a figure here is out of date, the sources are the reference.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Which gap would you want counted first?

scenes.title: The count
scenes.place: A paper ledger on a wooden desk, one huge number written across the page

scenes.title: Before
scenes.place: A wall chart in a quiet office, a small stack of species cards pinned in one corner

scenes.title: What is in it
scenes.place: Three large crates on a loading dock, one marked animals, one plants, one fungi

scenes.title: Used or traded
scenes.place: Two overlapping circles chalked on a classroom blackboard, one word in each

scenes.title: Not a doubling of trade
scenes.place: A long table of database folders, a magnifying glass resting on one of them

scenes.title: The gaps
scenes.place: A harbour warehouse with shelves of labelled boxes and one empty shelf marked with a question mark

scenes.title: Watching
scenes.place: A dashboard with a long bar that is almost entirely grey, a thin bright sliver at one end

scenes.title: What is uncertain
scenes.place: A tray of unfinished puzzle pieces beside a half-built picture of a map

scenes.title: Proposals
scenes.place: A tidy desk with a laptop, a stamped paper permit and a scanner side by side

scenes.title: Still unknown
scenes.place: The same ledger on the same wooden desk, the huge number now with a blank line under it
